Slovakia’s Steel Sector Posts Steady Growth Amid Stable Market Conditions

The Slovak steel industry reported steady performance in the latest quarterly results, reflecting stable demand and continued operational efficiency across the sector. Major producers in the country, including Slovenské Oceliarne and Východoslovenský Metal, cited increased output and improved margins, bolstered by resilient construction and automotive sectors.

According to data released by the Slovak Steel Association on Thursday, total crude steel production in Slovakia reached 1.18 million tonnes in the first quarter of 2024, marking a year-on-year increase of 2.5%. Revenue across the industry rose modestly by 3.1% to €1.7 billion, as higher average selling prices offset increased energy and input costs.

“Slovakia’s steel industry continues to demonstrate resilience in a challenging European environment,” said Jana Hrušková, president of the Slovak Steel Association. “We are seeing stable orders from both domestic and export customers, particularly in construction and machinery manufacturing.”

Slovenské Oceliarne, the nation’s largest steelmaker, reported a 2% year-on-year rise in shipments, with CEO Martin Gregor noting, “We have successfully navigated fluctuating raw material prices and maintained strong relationships with our key clients in the region.” He added that efficiency measures implemented last year have helped offset higher energy costs.

Export activity remains robust, with nearly 78% of Slovakia’s steel output destined for markets in Central and Western Europe. “Our export levels are holding firm, supported by ongoing infrastructure investments in neighbouring countries,” said Tomáš Dvořák, head of strategy at Východoslovenský Metal.

Analysts say the performance reflects broader European trends, where moderate demand recovery and supply chain normalization are supporting steelmakers. “The Slovak steel sector is benefiting from a stable macroeconomic backdrop, with no major disruptions to supply or demand,” observed Lucia Sýkorová, an industry analyst at Bratislava-based consultancy TrendMetals.

Employment in the sector remained stable, with around 9,500 workers employed across Slovakia’s steel mills. The Metalworkers’ Union welcomed the results, with union chair Jozef Mikuš stating, “The continued stability provides security for our members and their families.”

Looking ahead, industry leaders expect similar conditions to persist. “While we are vigilant regarding energy prices and global market developments, we remain optimistic for the coming quarters,” said Hrušková.

The steel industry remains a key pillar of Slovakia’s industrial economy, contributing significantly to exports and regional development. As global supply chains continue to recover, sector executives anticipate continued steady performance in the months ahead.
